newsitem.title: USA: Pan Am in talks for building.
newsitem.headline: Pan Am in talks for building.

text.p: Pan Am Corp Chairman Charles Cobb said Friday the company was in talks with what remains of Eastern Airlines to acquire the building in the outskirts of Miami where Pan Am is headquartered in exchange for Pan Am stock.

"It would give Eastern a bit more than 10 percent (of Pan Am's outstanding stock)," Cobb told Reuters after a news conference in which company executives discussed Pan Am's proposed acquisition of Carnival Air Lines.

Cobb said the sale was in the discussion phase, and depended on factors including Pan Am's finalizing an arrangement with the government of Dade County in which it promised to keep its headquarters in Miami.

If the Carnival acquisition went through, Carnival's principle owner, Micky Arison, would end up with about 42 percent of Pan Am's stock. Much of the 10 to 12 percent of Pan Am that would end up with Eastern after the headquarters deal would come from Arison's stake, Cobb said.
Eastern Airlines, once South Florida's premier airline, shut down in 1991 after a crippling strike and a mountain of debt forced it into bankruptcy.
